questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text:
Consider the following statements about sympathetic, parasympathetic, and motor nerves. Which of the following statements are true?

1. Sympathetic efferents are distributed all over the body/ extensively whereas parasympathetic distribution is limited.
2. Sympathetic fibers travel long distances after leaving the sympathetic chain, before finally synapsing and then a shorter distance to effector organs.
3. Parasympathetic fibers travel a shorter distance to their respective ganglia which are located close to the target organs.
4. Motor neurons are located in the ventral horn of the spinal cord from where the axons come out and divide into several branches, each of which supplies an individual muscle fiber.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1,4

The true statements are 1,4.

Sympathetic efferents are distributed extensively all over the body whereas parasympathetic distribution is limited to head, neck, and trunk regions.

Sympathetic fibers travel short distances to the sympathetic ganglionic chain, before finally synapsing and then have a long course to supply the target organs. Parasympathetic fibers travel a longer distance to their respective ganglia which are located close to the target organs.

Motor neurons are located in the ventral horn of the spinal cord from where the axons come out and divide into several branches, each of which supplies an individual muscle fiber. A motor unit comprises a motor neuron and a group of skeletal muscle fibers it innervates.
questions.learning: Sympathetic efferents are distributed extensively all over the body whereas parasympathetic distribution is limited to head, neck, and trunk regions. Sympathetic fibers travel short distances to the sympathetic ganglionic chain, before finally synapsing…

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A patient with splenic trauma is being treated conservatively. Certain findings on contrast- enhanced CT may indicate the need for further intervention, such as angiography. Which of the following CT scan findings would not usually warrant angiography during conservative management of splenic injury?
questions.explanation: In the conservative (non-operative) management of splenic trauma, angiography and embolization are targeted toward signs of active bleeding or vascular instability. Findings such as a pseudoaneurysm (Option C) and active contrast extravasation (Option D) are high-risk indicators of impending or ongoing hemorrhage and almost always require angiography. Significant hemoperitoneum (Option B) can also be a marker for vascular injury requiring intervention. However, a subcapsular hematoma (Option A), even one covering 40% of the surface area (Class II injury), is a localized, contained collection of blood. As long as the patient remains hemodynamically stable, this finding is traditionally managed with strict bed rest and serial imaging rather than invasive angiography. Therefore, a contained subcapsular hematoma is the "least" concerning vascular finding among the choices provided and does not mandate an immediate angiographic procedure
questions.learning: In the conservative (non-operative) management of splenic trauma, angiography and embolization are targeted toward signs of active bleeding or vascular instability.

questions.text: A 49-year-old man returns for follow-up after being recently diagnosed with a condition and started on treatment. During counseling, he is informed about the Axshya project. This project is associated with the management and control of which disease?
questions.explanation: The Axshya Project is a large public health initiative in India aimed at improving the control and elimination of tuberculosis (TB). It is implemented by the The Union with support from the Global Fund. The project focuses on: 1. Active case finding in vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations 2. Awareness and advocacy about TB symptoms and treatment 3. Reducing stigma and discrimination associated with TB 4. Strengthening community participation and early diagnosis Its goal aligns with India’s mission to eliminate TB by improving early detection, treatment adherence, and reporting. Why other options are incorrect: (B) Diabetes → No relation to Axshya project (C) Malaria → Covered under separate national programs (D) Zika infection → Managed under vector-borne disease control programs

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
A student was making a presentation with charts but lost titles while editing. What could be the heading for the following chart?

Parameters
Data

Mean life expectancy at birth
67.7 years

Expected years of schooling
12.6 years

Mean years of schooling
10.6 years

Gross national income per capita
USD 6951
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Human Development Index

The index that is calculated using the given indicators such as life expectancy at birth, mean and expected years of schooling, and the per capita income is the Human Developmental Index (HDI).

Human Development Index (HDI) is defined as a composite index focusing on three basic dimensions of human development. It assesses abilities

• To lead a healthy long life - measured by life expectancy at birth
• To acquire knowledge- measured by mean years of schooling
• To achieve a decent standard of living- measured by gross national income per capita

Hence the 3 dimension indices used to calculate the human development index are as follows life expectancy index, education index, and gross national index.

Other options:

Option A- Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) uses three indicators which include infant mortality, life expectancy at age one, and literacy rate.

Option B- Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) - It is an international measure of acute multidimensional poverty by capturing the acute deprivations in health, education, and living standards that a person faces simultaneously. It is assessed using 3 dimensions and 10 indicators which are as follows:

1. Health - Nutrition and child mortality
2. Education- Years of schooling and school attendance
3. Standard of living -

• Cooking fuel
• Sanitation
• Drinking water
• Electricity
• Housing
• Assets

Option C- Disability-adjusted life years (DALY): It is the amount of time lost due to ill health. It is expressed as the number of years lost due to ill-health, disability, or early death. The components of DALY are:

• Years of life lost due to premature death
• Years lived with disability (YLD)
• Years lived in a state less than full health
questions.learning: Human Development Index — The index that is calculated using the given indicators such as life expectancy at birth, mean and expected years of schooling, and the per capita income is the Human Developmental Index (HDI).
